label: t:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{t:main}
Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 4$ with $V_F^{*} = \{ \mathbf{0} \}$.
Suppose
$$
n \geqslant 24  d^4  2^{d}.
$$
Suppose further that the equation $F(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ has a nonsingular real solution in $(0,1)^{n}$, and also
has a nonsingular solution in $( \mathbb{Z}_p^{\times} )^n$ for every prime $p$.
Then
$$
N_F(P) \gg P^{n - d}.
$$
head: environment

label: t:asymptotic
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{t:asymptotic}
Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 4$ with $V_F^{*} = \{ \mathbf{0} \}$.
Suppose
$$
n \geqslant (24 (d-1)^2 d^2 + 7 (d-1) ) 2^{d} + 11.
$$
Suppose further that the equation $F(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ has a nonsingular real solution in $(0,1)^{n}$, and also
has a nonsingular solution in $( \mathbb{Z}_p^{\times} )^n$ for every prime $p$.
Let $\mathbf{x}_0$, $\delta$, $\omega$ and $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n$ be as in this section.
Then, for any $A > 0$, we have
\[
\sum_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\prod_{i=1}^n\psi_i(x_i)\Lambda(x_i)
\cdot\mathbbm{1}_{V(F)}(\mathbf{x})
= c(F;\omega,\mathbf{x}_0)P^{n-d}
+O\left(\frac{P^{n-d}}{(\log P)^A}\right),
\]
where $c(F;\omega,\mathbf{x}_0)>0$ is a constant depending only on $F, \omega$ and $\mathbf{x}_0$.
head: environment

label: lem:Weyl
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Weyl}
Let $d\geqslant3$, $X\geqslant1$, and let
\[
 f(x)=\theta x^d+\theta_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+\theta_1x\in\mathbb{R}[x].
\]
Let $a \in\mathbb{Z}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\gcd(a,q)=1$.
Then
\begin{equation*}                       
 \sum_{1 \leqslant x \leqslant X} e(f(x))
 \ll X^{1+\varepsilon}
 \bigl(X^{-1}+\lambda^{-1}+\lambda X^{-d}\bigr)^{ \frac{1}{d(d-1)}},
\end{equation*}
where $\lambda= q+ X^d|q\theta-a|$, for any $\varepsilon > 0$. Here the implicit constant is independent of $\theta_{d-1}, \cdots, \theta_{1}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As a consequence of Vinogradov's mean value theorem, it is known (for example, this is recorded in~\cite[Lemma~2.4]{browning-yamagishi}) that
given any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}$ such that  $\gcd(a,q) = 1$, $|\theta - a/q| \leqslant q^{-2}$ and $q \leqslant X^d$, we have
$$
\sum_{1 \leqslant x \leqslant X} e(f(x))
\ll X^{1+\varepsilon}
\bigl(X^{-1}+ q^{-1}+ q X^{-d}\bigr)^{ \frac{1}{d(d-1)} }.
$$
The condition $q \leqslant X^d$ is superfluous, because the bound holds trivially if $q > X^d$.
Furthermore, it can be seen from the proof, given in~\cite[Theorem~5.2]{vaughan} and~\cite[Theorem~1.5]{wooleyMVT}, that the implicit constant is independent of
$\theta_{d-1}, \cdots, \theta_{1}$. Thus, the result follows on applying~\cite[Lemma~14.1]{wooley}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: By simply shifting the polynomial $f$, we can see that the bound in this lemma holds even if the range of summation $[1, X]$ is replaced with any other interval of length $\ll X$.
head: environment

label: TypeII
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{TypeII}
Let $d\geqslant3$, and let
\[
f(x)=\theta x^d+\theta_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+\theta_1x\in\mathbb{R}[x].
\]
Let $\gamma > 0$, $1\leqslant Q\leqslant P^{1/4}$, $P \ll X \leqslant P$, $P^{1/8} \leqslant M, N \leqslant P$ and $P \ll M N \ll P$.
Let us define
$$
\mathcal{S} = \sum_{ N \leqslant  y <  2 N } \sum_{ \substack{ M \leqslant x <  2 M \\ \gamma P \leqslant  x y \leqslant  X } } \xi_1(x) \xi_2(y) e( f(xy) ),
$$
where $|\xi_1(m)|, |\xi_2(m)| \ll m^{\varepsilon}$ for all $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $\varepsilon > 0$. If $\theta\notin\mathfrak M(Q)$,
then
$$
\mathcal{S} \ll  P^{1 + \varepsilon} Q^{- \frac{1}{2 d (d-1)}},
$$
for any $\varepsilon > 0$.
head: environment

label: lem:prime-Weyl
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:prime-Weyl}
Let $d\geqslant3$, and let
\[
f(x)=\theta x^d+\theta_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+\theta_1x\in\mathbb{R}[x].
\]
Let $\gamma > 0$.
If $\theta\notin\mathfrak M(Q)$, $1\leqslant Q\leqslant P^{1/4}$ and $P \ll X \leqslant P$, then
\begin{equation*}                      
\sum_{\gamma P \leqslant x\leqslant X}\Lambda(x)e(f(x)) \ll P^{1+\varepsilon}Q^{- \frac{1}{2d(d-1)} },
\end{equation*}
for any $\varepsilon > 0$.
head: environment

label: eq:mixed-height
title: Proof
body_md:
By Dirichlet's theorem, there exist $a\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\gcd(a,q)=1$,
\[
1\leqslant q\leqslant P^{\frac{d}{2}}
\qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
|q\theta-a|\leqslant P^{- \frac{d}{2}}.
\]
Since $\theta\notin\mathfrak M(Q)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-height}
 Q<q+P^d|q\theta-a|\leqslant2P^{\frac{d}{2}}.
\end{equation}
Let us define
\[
 A(y)=\sum_{\substack{rs=y\\ 1 \leqslant r,s\leqslant U}}\mu(r)\Lambda(s)
\qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
 B(y)=\sum_{\substack{r\mid y\\ 1 \leqslant  r\leqslant U}}\mu(r),
\]
where $U=P^{1/8}$. We apply Vaughan's identity~\cite[Section~24]{davenport} to decompose the sum into Type I and Type II sums as follows
\begin{equation}
\label{SSS+++}
\sum_{\gamma P \leqslant x \leqslant X}\Lambda(x)e(f(x)) = T_{\mathrm{I}}-T_{\mathrm{II}},
\end{equation}
where
\[
 T_{\mathrm{I}}=\sum_{1 \leqslant y \leqslant U}\mu(y)
 \sum_{ \gamma P/y \leqslant x \leqslant X/y   }(\log x)e(f(xy))- \sum_{1 \leqslant y \leqslant U^2} A(y)
 \sum_{ \gamma P/y \leqslant x \leqslant X/y  }e(f(xy))
\]
and
\[
T_{\mathrm{II}}=\sum_{ U <  y  \leqslant X } B(y) \sum_{  \substack{ U <  x \leqslant X /y   \\  \gamma P \leqslant xy  } }\Lambda(x)e(f(xy)).
\]
Here $|A(y)|\leqslant\log y$ and $|B(y)|\leqslant\tau(y)$, where $\tau(y)$ is the number of divisors of $y$.

For each $1 \leqslant y \leqslant U^2$, write $ay^d / q = b_y/r_y$ with $r_y \geqslant 1$ and $\gcd(b_y,r_y)=1$.
Let
\[
 \lambda_y = r_y +   \frac{ P^d |r_y  y^d \theta - b_y |}{y^d} =\frac{q+P^d|q\theta-a|}{\gcd(q,y^d)}.
\]
Let $0 < \sigma \leqslant 1 / d$ and $\iota \in \{1, 2 \}$. It follows from \eqref{eq:mixed-height} that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-height-moments1--}
\lambda_y \leqslant \frac{q  +   P^{d} |q \theta  - a|  }{\gcd(q, y^d)} \leqslant 2 P^{\frac{d}{2}}.
\end{equation}
Similarly, since it follows from \eqref{eq:mixed-height} that
$$
\frac{Q}{2} < q \qquad \textnormal{or} \qquad \frac{Q}{2} < P^d |q  \theta  - a|,
$$
we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{eq:mixed-height-moments2--}
\sum_{ M \leqslant y < 2 M }\lambda_y^{-\sigma}
&\ll&
\sum_{ M \leqslant y < 2 M } \frac{\gcd(q, y^d)^{\sigma}}{ Q^{\sigma} }
\\
\notag
&\ll&
\sum_{\ell |  q}  Q^{- \sigma}  \sum_{g | \ell}  \sum_{ \substack{ M \leqslant y < 2 M  \\ \gcd(q, y^d) = \ell  \\ \gcd(q, y) = g  } }
\ell^{\sigma}
\\
\notag
&\ll&
\tau(q) \sum_{\ell |  q}  Q^{- \sigma} \ell^{\sigma} \frac{M}{ \ell^{1/d} }
\\
\notag
&\ll&
M Q^{- \sigma} \tau(q)^2.
\end{eqnarray}
Therefore, by Lemma~\ref{lem:Weyl} (with partial summation when $\iota = 1$), \eqref{eq:mixed-height-moments1--} and \eqref{eq:mixed-height-moments2--}, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{typeI}
T_{\mathrm{I}} &\ll&  \sum_{\iota \in \{1, 2\} } (\log P) \sum_{1 \leqslant y \leqslant U^{\iota}}
\left|   \sum_{ \gamma P /y \leqslant x \leqslant X/y} (\log x)^{2 - \iota}  e(f(xy)) \right|
\\
\notag
&\ll&
(\log P)^2 \sum_{1 \leqslant y \leqslant U^2 }
\frac{X^{1+ \varepsilon}}{ y^{1 + \varepsilon }}  \left(   \frac{y}{X} + \lambda_y^{-1}+\lambda_y \frac{y^d}{X^d}  \right)^{ \frac{1}{d(d-1)}}
\\
\notag
&\ll&
(\log P)^2
X^{1 - \frac{1}{d(d-1)} +  \varepsilon} U^{ \frac{ 2}{d(d-1)}  }
\\
\notag
&&
+ (\log P)^3  X^{1 + \varepsilon}
\sup_{ \substack{  [M, 2M) \subseteq [1, U^2] \\ M \geqslant 1 }}
\bigl( Q^{- \frac{1}{d(d-1)}} \tau(q)^2 +
M^{\frac{1}{d-1}} X^{- \frac{1}{d-1}} P^{\frac{1}{2 (d-1)}} \bigr)
\\
\notag
&\ll& P^{1+\varepsilon} \bigl(    Q^{-  \frac{1}{d(d-1)}   } +  P^{-  \frac{1}{4(d-1)} }    \bigr).
\end{eqnarray}

We treat $T_{\mathrm{II}}$ by decomposing it into dyadic sums as follows
\begin{eqnarray*}
T_{\mathrm{II}}
&\ll&
(\log P)^2 \sup \sum_{ \substack{ N \leqslant y < 2 N  \\  U <  y  \leqslant X  }} B(y) \sum_{ \substack{  M \leqslant x < 2 M  \\   U <  x \leqslant X /y \\ \gamma P \leqslant x y } }\Lambda(x) e(f(xy)),
\end{eqnarray*}
where the supremum is over $[M,2M)$ and  $[N, 2N)$ with  $U \leqslant M, N \leqslant X$ and $P \ll M N \ll P$.
Then, by Lemma~\ref{TypeII}, we obtain
$$
T_{\mathrm{II}} \ll  P^{1 + 2 \varepsilon} Q^{- \frac{1}{2 d (d-1)}}.
$$
Finally, on substituting this estimate and \eqref{typeI} into \eqref{SSS+++}, it follows that
$$
\sum_{ \gamma P  \leqslant x \leqslant X}\Lambda(x) e(f(x)) \ll  |T_{\mathrm{I}}| + |T_{\mathrm{II}}|  \ll  P^{1 +  \varepsilon} Q^{- \frac{1}{2 d (d-1)}}.
$$
head: environment

label: lem:pure-terminal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pure-terminal}
Suppose  $P^{1/100}\leqslant L\leqslant P^{d/2}$ and $\alpha\in\mathfrak n(L)$. Then
\begin{equation*}                         
 \sum_{1 \leqslant x \leqslant P} \omega_1 \left( \frac{x}{P} \right) \Lambda(x) \,  e\bigl(\Phi(x)\bigr)
\ll P^{1 + \varepsilon} L^{-  \frac{1}{ 4d^2(d-1)  } },
\end{equation*}
for any $\varepsilon > 0$. Here the implicit constant is independent of the coefficients of $\Phi(x) - c \alpha x^d$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\alpha\notin\mathfrak M(L)$, we have $c \alpha \notin \mathfrak M(L/|c|)$.
If $P^{1/4} \leqslant L/|c|$, then it follows that $c \alpha \notin \mathfrak M(P^{1/4})$.
Let $Q = \min\{L/|c|,P^{1/4}\}$. Let $\gamma > 0$ be sufficiently small.
Therefore, by partial summation and Lemma~\ref{lem:prime-Weyl}, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\left| \sum_{1 \leqslant x \leqslant P} \omega_1 \left( \frac{x}{P} \right) \Lambda(x) \,  e\bigl(\Phi(x)\bigr) \right|
&=&
P^{-1} \left| \int_{1}^P  \omega_1' \left( \frac{t}{P} \right)   \sum_{\gamma P  \leqslant x \leqslant t}  \Lambda(x) \,   e\bigl(\Phi(x)\bigr) \mathrm{d} t \right|
\\
&\ll&
P^{1 + \varepsilon} Q^{- \frac{1}{2d(d-1)}}
\\
&\ll&
\begin{cases}
P^{1 + \varepsilon} L^{- \frac{1}{2d(d-1)}} & \mbox{if } P^{1/100}  \leqslant L  \leqslant |c|P^{1/4},  \\
P^{ 1 + \varepsilon  -  \frac{1}{8d(d-1)}} & \mbox{if } |c|P^{1/4}< L \leqslant P^{d/2}.
\end{cases}
\end{eqnarray*}
In either case, we obtain the bound
$$
\ll P^{1 + \varepsilon} L^{-  \frac{1}{ 4d^2(d-1)  } },
$$
which proves the lemma.
head: environment

label: lem:mixed-terminal
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:mixed-height+
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\alpha\in\mathfrak M(2L)$, there exist $a_0 \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\gcd(a_0,q_0)=1$, $1\leqslant q_0\leqslant2L$ and $P^d|q_0\alpha-a_0|\leqslant2L$.
Write $ca_0/q_0=a/q$ with $q\geqslant1$ and $\gcd(a,q)=1$.                                                  
Then it follows that
$$
1 \leqslant q \leqslant 2L \qquad \textnormal{and} \qquad P^d|q c \alpha - a|\leqslant 2 |c| L.
$$
Since $c \alpha \notin \mathfrak M(L/|c|)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-height+}
\frac{L}{|c|} < q +  P^d |q c \alpha  - a| \ll L.
\end{equation}
For each $1\leqslant h\leqslant P$, write $ah/q = b_h/r_h$ with $r_h\geqslant1$ and $\gcd(b_h,r_h)=1$, and put
\[
\lambda_h=r_h+P^{d-1}|r_h h c \alpha - b_h|
 =\frac{q  +   hP^{d-1} |q c \alpha   - a|  }{\gcd(q,h)}.
\]

Let $0 < \sigma < 1$. It follows from \eqref{eq:mixed-height+} that
$$
\lambda_h \leqslant \frac{q  +   P^{d} |q c \alpha   - a|  }{\gcd(q,h)} \ll L.
$$
Therefore, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-height-moments1}
\sum_{1 \leqslant h\leqslant P} \lambda_h^\sigma \ll P L^\sigma.
\end{equation}
Similarly, since it follows from \eqref{eq:mixed-height+} that
$$
\frac{L}{2|c|} < q \qquad \textnormal{or} \qquad \frac{L}{2|c|} < P^d |q c \alpha  - a|,
$$
we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{eq:mixed-height-moments2}
\sum_{1 \leqslant h\leqslant P}\lambda_h^{-\sigma}
&\ll&
\sum_{1 \leqslant h\leqslant P}
\left( \frac{\gcd(q,h)^{\sigma}}{L^{\sigma}} + \frac{\gcd(q,h)^{\sigma} P^{\sigma}}{ h^{\sigma} L^{\sigma}  } \right)
\\
\notag
&\ll&
\sum_{\ell |  q} \ell^{\sigma} L^{- \sigma} \sum_{ \substack{ 1 \leqslant h\leqslant P \\ \gcd(h, q) = \ell  } }
\left( 1 + \frac{ P^{\sigma}}{ h^{\sigma} } \right)
\\
\notag
&\ll&
\sum_{\ell | q } \ell^{\sigma} L^{- \sigma } \frac{P}{\ell }
\\
\notag
&\ll& P L^{-\sigma} \tau(q)
\\
\notag
&\ll& P^{1 + \varepsilon} L^{-\sigma}.
\end{eqnarray}

Let
\[
S = \sum_{ 1 \leqslant  x \leqslant P }\sum_{ 1 \leqslant  y \leqslant P} \omega_1 \left( \frac{x}{P} \right) \omega_2 \left( \frac{y}{P} \right) \Lambda(x) \, \Lambda(y) \, e\bigl(\Phi(x,y)\bigr).
\]
Let $\gamma > 0$ be sufficiently small.
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
|S|^2 &\ll&  P (\log P)^2  \sum_{ \gamma P \leqslant  x \leqslant P } \sum_{ 1 \leqslant  y_1, y_2 \leqslant P}
\\
&&  \omega_2 \left( \frac{y_1}{P} \right) \omega_2 \left( \frac{y_2}{P} \right) \Lambda(y_1) \, \Lambda(y_2) \, e\bigl(\Phi(x,y_1) - \Phi(x,y_2)\bigr)
\\
&\ll& P^3 (\log P)^4 +  P (\log P)^4 \sum_{ \substack{ 1 \leqslant y_1,  y_2 \leqslant P \\ y_1 \neq y_2  } }
\\
&&
\left| \sum_{\gamma P  \leqslant x \leqslant P}  e\bigl(  c \alpha (y_1 - y_2) x^{d-1} + \nu(x, y_1, y_2)  \bigr) \right|,
\end{eqnarray*}
where
$$
\nu(x, y_1, y_2) = \Phi(x,y_1) -  c \alpha y_1  x^{d-1}  - \Phi(x,y_2) + c \alpha y_2  x^{d-1}.
$$
In particular, $\deg_x \nu \leqslant d - 2$. Therefore, it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:Weyl}, \eqref{eq:mixed-height-moments1} and \eqref{eq:mixed-height-moments2} that
\begin{eqnarray*}
|S|^2 &\ll&  P^3 (\log P)^4 +  P^2 (\log P)^4 \sum_{1 \leqslant h \leqslant P} P^{1+ \varepsilon}  \bigl(P^{-1}+\lambda_h^{-1}+\lambda_h P^{-d + 1}\bigr)^{ \frac{1}{(d-1)(d-2)}}
\\
&\ll&
P^{3 + 2 \varepsilon}
\left( P^{1 - \frac{1}{(d-1)(d-2)} } + P^{1 + \varepsilon}  L^{- \frac{1}{(d-1)(d-2)}} + L^{ \frac{1}{(d-1)(d-2)}} P^{ 1 -  \frac{1}{ d-2 }} \right)
\\
&\ll&
P^{4 + 2 \varepsilon} L^{- \frac{2}{d (d-1)(d-2) }},
\end{eqnarray*}
where the final inequality follows on recalling that $P^{1/100}\leqslant L\leqslant P^{d/2}$ and $d\geqslant4$.
The lemma then follows by taking the square roots.
head: environment

label: t:minor
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{t:minor}
Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 4$ with $V_F^{*} = \{ \mathbf{0} \}$.
Suppose
$$
n \geqslant (24 (d-1)^2 d^2 + 7 (d-1) ) 2^{d} + 11.
$$
Let $S(\alpha)$ be as in \eqref{defS}, and let $Q_0 = P^{1/100}$. Let $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq \mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}$ be a measurable set.
Then there exists $\delta > 0$ such that
$$
\int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap  ((\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}) \setminus \mathfrak{M}(Q_0) ) } S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha \ll P^{n - d- \delta}.
$$
head: environment

label: LZ
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The assumption that $F$ defines a smooth hypersurface is not necessary for this proposition.
Also, the weights of the exponential sum $S(\alpha)$ satisfy
$$
| \psi_i(x) \Lambda (x) | \leqslant \log x \qquad (x \in [1,P] \cap \mathbb{Z})
$$
for all $1 \leqslant i \leqslant n$, which is sufficient to apply~\cite[Proposition~5.1]{liuzhao} $($see~\cite[pp.8625]{liuzhao}$)$.
head: environment

label: LEMMA2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{LEMMA2}
Suppose
$$
m - \dim V_f^*  > \left(  \frac{1}{\varrho} + \frac{1}{2}  \right)   (d-1) 2^{d + 1}
$$
and
$$
m + s - \dim V_g^*  > \left(  \frac{1}{2 \varrho} +  \frac{3}{4}  \right)  (d-1) 2^{d + 2}.
$$
Suppose further that, for any $\varepsilon_0 > 0$ sufficiently small, we have
$$
W(L) \ll P^{t + \varepsilon_0} L^{- \varrho}
$$
for any $P^{1/100} \leqslant L \leqslant P^{d/2}$. Then there exists $\delta > 0$ such that
$$
\int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap \mathfrak{n}(L) } S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha \ll P^{n - d }   (\log P)^{2n}  L^{-\delta}
$$
holds for any measurable $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq \mathbb{R}/ \mathbb{Z}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta_0 > 0$ be sufficiently small, and let $0 <  \varepsilon_0 <  \delta_0 / 100$.
We set
$$
X =  L^{\frac{\varrho}{2}  - \delta_0 } \leqslant \frac{1}{4}P^{\frac{d}{2}}.
$$
Let
$$
m - \dim V_f^*  \geqslant \kappa_1 \qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
m + s - \dim V_g^*  \geqslant \kappa_2
$$
for some $\kappa_1, \kappa_2 > (d-1) 2^d$.
Let us recall from \eqref{measnL} that
$$
|\mathfrak{n}(L)| \ll L^{2} P^{ -d}.
$$
Then it follows from Proposition~\ref{LZ} that
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                     
\int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap \mathfrak{n}(L) } S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha  &\ll&  P^{n - \frac{d}{2}}   (\log P)^{2n}  X^{1 - \frac{   \kappa_1 }{ (d-1) 2^d  } } L P^{- \frac{d}{2}}
\label{mean}
\\
\notag
&&+ P^{ n - \frac{3d}{4} }   (\log P)^{2n}  X^{\frac{3}{2} - \frac{   \kappa_2 }{ (d-1) 2^{d+1}  } } L^{\frac{1}{2}} P^{- \frac{d}{4}}
\\
\notag
&&+ P^{ m + s - d }   (\log P)^{m + s}  X^{2}  W(L).
\end{eqnarray}
Therefore, if
$$
\frac{ \varrho  \kappa_1 }{ (d-1) 2^{d+1}  }  >  1 +  \frac{\varrho}{2}
\qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
\frac{ \varrho  \kappa_2 }{ (d-1) 2^{d+2} }  >  \frac{1}{2} + \frac{3 \varrho}{4},
$$
or equivalently,
$$
\kappa_1 >   \left(  \frac{1}{\varrho} + \frac{1}{2}  \right)   (d-1) 2^{d + 1}
\qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
\kappa_2  >   \left(  \frac{1}{2 \varrho} +  \frac{3}{4}  \right)  (d-1) 2^{d + 2},
$$
then \eqref{mean} becomes
\begin{eqnarray*}
\int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap   \mathfrak{n}(L) } S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha
&\ll&
P^{n - d }    (\log P)^{2n}  L^{-\varepsilon} + P^{ n - t - d }   (\log P)^{n - t}  X^{2}  W(L)
\\
&\ll&
P^{n - d }    (\log P)^{2n}  L^{-\varepsilon} + P^{ n - t - d }   (\log P)^{n - t}  L^{\varrho - 2 \delta_0}  W(L)
\\
&\ll&
P^{n - d }    (\log P)^{2n}  L^{-\varepsilon} + P^{ n - d }   (\log P)^{n - t}  L^{- 2 \delta_0}  P^{\varepsilon_0}
\\
&\ll&
P^{n - d }    (\log P)^{2n}  L^{-\varepsilon},
\end{eqnarray*}
for some $\varepsilon > 0$.
head: environment

label: smooth
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{smooth}
Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 2$ such that $V_F^* = \{ \mathbf{0} \}$.
Then either there exists $1 \leqslant i \leqslant n$ such that $x_i^d$ has a nonzero coefficient in $F$,
or there exist $1 \leqslant j, k \leqslant n$ such that $x_j^{d-1} x_k$ has a nonzero coefficient.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $2 \leqslant k \leqslant n$, let $C_k$ denote the coefficient of $x_{1}^{d-1} x_k$ in $F$.
Then
$$
\frac{ \partial F}{ \partial x_k }(1, 0, \ldots, 0) = \begin{cases}
                                                       d F(1, 0, \ldots, 0)  & \mbox{if } k = 1,  \\
                                                       C_k  & \mbox{if } 2 \leqslant k \leqslant n.
                                                      \end{cases}
$$
Therefore, if the coefficients of $x_i^d$  and $x_j^{d-1} x_k$  in $F$ are zero for all $1 \leqslant i, j, k \leqslant n$,
then this leads to
$$
(1, 0, \ldots, 0) \in V_F^*,
$$
which is a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We begin by partitioning the variables in a way that Lemma~\ref{LEMMA2} is applicable.
If we are in the first case of Lemma~\ref{smooth}, i.e.  there exists $1 \leqslant i \leqslant n$ such that $x_i^d$ has a nonzero coefficient in $F$,
then we assume without loss of generality that $i = n$, and set $\mathbf{w} = x_n$. In this case, it follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:pure-terminal} that
$$
W(L) \ll P^{t + \varepsilon_0} L^{- \varrho},
$$
for any $P^{1/100} \leqslant L \leqslant P^{d/2}$. On the other hand, if we are not in the first case of Lemma~\ref{smooth},
i.e. there exist $1 \leqslant j, k \leqslant n$ such that $x_j^{d-1} x_k$ has a nonzero coefficient in $F$
while the coefficient of $x_i^d$ is zero for all $1 \leqslant i \leqslant n$, then we assume without loss of generality
that $(j, k) = (n-1, n)$, and set $\mathbf{w} = (x_{n-1}, x_n)$. In this case, it follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed-terminal} that
$$
W(L) \ll P^{t + \varepsilon_0} L^{- \varrho},
$$
for any $P^{1/100} \leqslant L \leqslant P^{d/2}$. Thus, we see that in either case the upper
bound on $W(L)$ required in Lemma~\ref{LEMMA2} is satisfied.


Since $V_F^*  = \{ \mathbf{0} \}$, it follows from~\cite[Lemma~3.1]{yamagishi} that
$$
\textnormal{codim }V_f^* \geqslant \textnormal{codim }V_F^* - 2(s + t) = n - 2 (s + t).
$$
Let
$$
V_1 = \left\{ \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{A}^n_\mathbb{C}:  \frac{\partial F }{\partial x_{1}} (\mathbf{x}) = \cdots = \frac{\partial F }{\partial x_{m}} (\mathbf{x})  = 0  \right\}
$$
and
$$
V_2 = \left\{ \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{A}^n_\mathbb{C}:  \frac{\partial F }{\partial x_{m+1}} (\mathbf{x})  = \cdots = \frac{\partial F }{\partial x_{n}} (\mathbf{x}) = 0  \right\}.
$$
Since these are affine varieties defined by homogeneous forms, it follows that
$$
0 = \dim V_F^* = \dim (V_1 \cap V_2) \geqslant \dim V_2 - m,
$$
i.e.
$$
\dim V_2 \leqslant m.
$$
On noting that
$$
\frac{\partial (F - f) }{ \partial x_i } (\mathbf{x}) = \frac{\partial F  }{ \partial x_i } (\mathbf{x}) \qquad (m + 1 \leqslant i \leqslant n),
$$
we have
$$
V_{F - f}^* \subseteq V_2.
$$
Hence,
$$
\textnormal{codim } V_{F - f}^* = n - \dim V_{F - f}^* \geqslant n - m.
$$
Therefore, it again follows from~\cite[Lemma~3.1]{yamagishi}  that
$$
\textnormal{codim } V_{g}^*  \geqslant \textnormal{codim } V_{F - f}^* - 2 t \geqslant n - m - 2t.
$$
Thus, the dimension requirements of Lemma~\ref{LEMMA2} are satisfied if
$$
n - 2(s + t)  \geqslant \left(  \frac{1}{\varrho} + \frac{1}{2}  \right)   (d-1) 2^{d + 1} + 1
$$
and
$$
n - m - 2t  =   (s + t) - 2t  \geqslant \left(  \frac{1}{2 \varrho} +  \frac{3}{4}  \right)  (d-1) 2^{d + 2} + 1.
$$
This means that provided
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{eq:nnn}
n - 4 t  &=& n - 2(s + t) + 2 (s + t) - 4t
\\
\notag
&\geqslant&
\left(  \frac{1}{\varrho} + \frac{1}{2}  \right)   (d-1) 2^{d + 1}
+ \left(  \frac{1}{\varrho} +  \frac{3}{2}  \right)  (d-1) 2^{d + 2} + 3
\\
\notag
&=&   \left(  \frac{6}{\varrho} +  7\right)     (d-1) 2^{d} + 3,
\end{eqnarray}
we may achieve\footnote{We can choose
$$
s  =    \left(  \frac{1}{2 \varrho} +  \frac{3}{4}  \right)  (d-1) 2^{d + 2} + t + 1 \qquad \textnormal{and} \qquad m = n - s - t.
$$}
the desired partition of the variables. Finally, since $t \in \{1, 2\}$, it is easy to see that \eqref{eq:nnn} holds given
$$
n \geqslant ( 24 (d-1) d^2 + 7) (d-1) 2^{d} + 11 = (24 (d-1)^2 d^2 + 7 (d-1) ) 2^{d} + 11.
$$

Let us recall from \eqref{dydshell} that
$$
(\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}) \setminus \mathfrak{M} (Q_0)
=  \bigcup_{1 \leqslant j \leqslant J} \mathfrak{n}(2^{j-1} Q_0).
$$
Therefore, given any measurable $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, by applying Lemma~\ref{LEMMA2}, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
\int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap ((\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}) \setminus \mathfrak{M} (Q_0) ) } S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha &=&  \sum_{j = 1}^{J} \int_{ \mathfrak{a} \cap  \mathfrak{n} ( 2^{j-1} Q_0)}   S(\alpha) \mathrm{d} \alpha
\\
&\ll&  P^{n - d }    (\log P)^{2n}  \sum_{j = 1}^J   (2^{j-1} Q_0)^{-\varepsilon}
\\
&\ll&  P^{n - d - \delta},
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\delta > 0$.
head: environment

label: lem:major-character
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:major-character}
Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 2$.
Let $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}$  be such that $\gcd(a,q)=1$.
Let $\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n$ be any Dirichlet characters modulo $q$, and let
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{calS}
\mathcal{S} (\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n) = \sum_{\mathbf{h} \in (\mathbb{Z}/q \mathbb{Z})^n  } \chi_1(h_1) \cdots \chi_n(h_n)
\ e \left( \frac{a}{q} F(h_1, \ldots, h_n)  \right).
\end{eqnarray}
Then, for any $\varepsilon > 0$, we have
$$
|\mathcal{S} (\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n) | \ll q^{n - \frac{ \textnormal{codim } V_{F}^* }{16(2d-1)}  + \varepsilon},
$$
where the implicit constant is independent of the choice of $\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n$.
head: environment

label: NGY
title: Proof
body_md:
We have the following bound recorded in the proof of~\cite[Theorem~D]{nguyen1},
which follows from~\cite[Theorem~C]{nguyen1} (or~\cite[Theorem~C]{nguyen} with the trivial weight $w = (1, \ldots, 1)$ and $r=1$) and the Chinese remainder theorem.
Let $H \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_N]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \geqslant 2$.
Let $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and  $q \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\gcd(a,q) = 1$.
Then, for any $\varepsilon > 0$ sufficiently small, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{NGY}
\sum_{\mathbf{x} \in (\mathbb{Z}/ q\mathbb{Z})^N} e \left(  \frac{a H(\mathbf{x})}{q} \right) \ll q^{N - \frac{\textnormal{codim } V_H^*}{2(d-1)} + \varepsilon }.
\end{equation}

It is shown in the proof of~\cite[Lemma~7.4]{yamagishi}, in~\cite[(7.10)]{yamagishi} to be precise, that
\begin{equation}
\label{CCSS}
|\mathcal{S} (\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n)|^4 \leqslant \sum_{\mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}' \in (\mathbb{Z}/ q \mathbb{Z})^n}
\sum_{\mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}' \in (\mathbb{Z}/ q \mathbb{Z})^n} e \left( \frac{a}{q} \mathfrak{D}( \mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}'  )  \right),
\end{equation}
where
$$
\mathfrak{D}( \mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}'  ) = G(\mathbf{h}; \mathbf{k}) - G(\mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}) - G(\mathbf{h}; \mathbf{k}') + G(\mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}')
$$
and
$$
G(\mathbf{h}; \mathbf{k}) = F(h_1k_1, \ldots h_n k_n).
$$
It is also shown in the same proof that
$$
\textnormal{codim } V_{\mathfrak{D}, 1}^* \geqslant \frac{\textnormal{codim } V_F^*}{2},
$$
where
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& V_{\mathfrak{D}, 1}^*
\\
&=& \left\{  (\mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}', \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}') \in \mathbb{A}^{4n}_{\mathbb{C}}: \frac{\partial \mathfrak{D}}{\partial h_i}  ( \mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}'  )  = \frac{\partial \mathfrak{D}}{\partial h'_i}  ( \mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}'; \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{k}'  )   =   0  \, \,  (1 \leqslant i \leqslant n) \right\}.
\end{eqnarray*}
   
                       
                          
                                              
                                                                  
                                                                    
                             
                        
   
Since
$$
V_{\mathfrak{D}}^* \subseteq V_{\mathfrak{D}, 1}^*,
$$
it follows that
$$
\textnormal{codim } V_{\mathfrak{D}}^* \geqslant \frac{\textnormal{codim } V_F^*}{2}.
$$
Therefore, by applying \eqref{NGY} to \eqref{CCSS}, we obtain
$$
|\mathcal{S} (\chi_1, \ldots, \chi_n)|^4 \ll q^{4n - \frac{\textnormal{codim } V_F^*}{4(2d-1)} + \varepsilon }.
$$
The lemma then follows by taking the fourth root.
head: environment

label: prop major
title: Proposition
body_md:
\cite[Proposition~3.1]{yamagishi2}
\label{prop major}
Let $F$, $\mathbf{x}_0$, $\delta$, $\omega$ and $\psi_1, \ldots, \psi_n$ be as in this section.
Suppose
$$
\textnormal{codim } V_F^* >  \max \left( 48(2d-1), (d-1) 2^{d}  + 4  (2 d - 1),   \frac{ (d-1) d 2^{d+2} }{  2d-1   }  \right).
$$
Let $\vartheta_0, \gamma, \lambda > 0$ be such that \eqref{theta0 major} is satisfied.
Then, for any $A > 0$, we have
$$
\int_{\mathfrak{M}^+(\vartheta_0; \lambda )} S(\alpha)   \mathrm{d} \alpha = c(F; \omega, \mathbf{x}_0)  P^{n-d} + O \left(  \frac{P^{n-d}}{(\log P)^A} \right),
$$
where $c(F; \omega, \mathbf{x}_0) > 0$ is a constant depending only on $F$, $\omega$ and $\mathbf{x}_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us set
$$
\vartheta_0 = \frac{1}{16} - \varepsilon,
\qquad
\lambda = \frac{1}{12}
\qquad
\textnormal{and}
\qquad
\gamma = \frac{7}{24}
$$
so that \eqref{theta0 major} is satisfied.
Since
$$
\frac{1}{100} \leqslant \vartheta_0,
$$
it is clear that
$$
\mathfrak{M} (Q_0) \subseteq  \mathfrak{M}^+ (\vartheta_0; \lambda),
$$
which implies
$$
\mathfrak{a} =  (\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}) \setminus  \mathfrak{M}^+ (\vartheta_0; \lambda) \subseteq   (\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}) \setminus \mathfrak{M} (Q_0).
$$
Therefore, by applying Theorem~\ref{t:minor} and Proposition~\ref{prop major}, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
\sum_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{Z}^n}  \prod_{i = 1}^n  \psi_i (x_i)  \Lambda(x_i)  \cdot \mathbbm{1}_{V(F)}(\mathbf{x})
&=& \int_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}  S(\alpha)   \mathrm{d} \alpha
\\
&=&
\int_{\mathfrak{M}^+(\vartheta_0; \lambda )} S(\alpha)   \mathrm{d} \alpha
+   \int_{ \mathfrak{a} } S(\alpha)   \mathrm{d} \alpha
\\
&=& c(F; \omega, \mathbf{x}_0) P^{n-d} + O \left(  \frac{P^{n-d}}{(\log P)^A} \right).
\end{eqnarray*}
